instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Mid-scale restaurant chain with 12 locations serving Mediterranean cuisine. Central kitchen produces 70% of menu items for distribution to satellite locations. Evaluating kitchen display systems, AI-driven prep quantity forecasting, and centralized procurement optimization. A growing organization that has moved past founder-led decision-making but is still building the formal processes and governance structures needed to scale. We have some digital tools in place but integration between systems is ad-hoc. Innovation is championed by 1-2 internal advocates.
answers.pastInitiatives: We piloted a cloud-based project management tool last year, but adoption was inconsistent across teams and we ultimately reverted to spreadsheets and email for most project tracking. The experience highlighted that tool adoption requires more structured change management than we initially planned for.
answers.strategicGoals: We are targeting a 20% improvement in operational throughput without increasing headcount. Our processes have grown organically over the years and are overdue for standardization. We suspect that workflow digitization, basic automation, and better data integration between our core systems can unlock significant productivity gains within our current cost structure.
answers.teamSize: We have a small technology team of 4-6 people including developers, a part-time DevOps engineer, and a product manager who also handles project management. The team is fully allocated to maintaining current products and handling integration requests from key clients. Innovation work is done in the margins — there is no formally ring-fenced innovation time or budget.

input.changes_since_last: Post-merger integration underway. Team doubled to 8 members. Culture clash between legacy and new teams.

opportunities.title: Cross-Functional Operational Process Mapping & Standardization
opportunities.rationale: The organization is undergoing a merger and has explicit needs for standardization to achieve 20% throughput improvement. Focusing on mapping the 'as-is' processes first will build the necessary consensus across legacy and new teams, addressing fundamental process gaps before attempting automation.

first_actions: Identify 3 high-volume cross-departmental workflows (e.g., order to kitchen prep).
Establish joint working groups comprising members from both legacy and new teams to map the existing process flow.
Document key pain points, manual handoffs, and decision bottlenecks for each workflow.
resources_needed: Executive sponsorship (Steering Committee) to enforce participation
execution_plan.success_metric: Completion of standardized process maps for 3 core operational workflows.
milestones: Phase 1: Workflow Identification & Stakeholder Buy-in (4 weeks)
Phase 2: Mapping & Gap Analysis Completion (6 weeks)

opportunities.title: Core System Data Layer Implementation
opportunities.rationale: The current system integration is ad-hoc, which severely limits data visibility and prevents basic automation. Implementing a foundational data layer (e.g., middleware or simple API gateway) will normalize critical data points across core systems without requiring immediate, high-cost replacement of existing tools.

first_actions: Identify the top 3 'core' datasets that must communicate (e.g., inventory, orders, labor hours).
Determine if a lightweight integration platform (iPaaS) or API wrapper is required to connect these systems.
Develop a proof-of-concept connecting only two critical data points.
execution_plan.success_metric: Successful, automated data transfer of 3 key metrics between identified systems.
milestones: Integration Build Completion for Test Dataset (8 weeks)

next_steps.action: Host a structured 'Process Alignment Workshop' involving representatives from both legacy and new teams to formally kick off the process mapping effort.
Conduct a detailed data inventory exercise to map every instance of manual data transfer and identify the specific API or connection point needed for automation.

key_weaknesses: Lack of formalized innovation bandwidth: Innovation efforts are confined to spare time, preventing sustained progress on structural changes.
Process Adherence Gap: Previous tool adoption failed due to insufficient change management and resistance across teams.
System Integration Fragmentation: Dependence on ad-hoc processes creates fragility and prevents full operational data utilization.

improvements: Increased human capital: Doubling the team size allows for dedicated, albeit limited, focus on process/tech initiatives.
Clearer strategic focus: The defined goal of 20% throughput improvement provides a quantifiable metric to drive change.
persistent_gaps: Organizational alignment and culture clash remains the primary barrier to standardized processes.
The lack of dedicated budget/time means opportunities remain marginalized rather than prioritized.
achieved_milestones: Identification of critical workflow pain points through self-assessment (survey data).

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The organization has doubled staffing and defined quantifiable efficiency goals (20% throughput). However, the core barriers—process standardization failure post-merger and ad-hoc systems integration—remain significant challenges that require a shift from general planning to structured process analysis.
